'''Joan Lasenby''' is a British physicist, engineer, and applied mathematician whose research interests include [[3D reconstruction]] and [[motion capture]], [[geometric algebra]], [[inverse kinematics]], and the applications of [[structured light plethysmography]] in non-invasive medical diagnostics. She is Professor of Image and Signal Analysis in the [[University of Cambridge]] Department of Engineering, and College Lecturer and Director of Studies in Engineering for [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].{{r|engcam}}

==Education and career==
Lasenby grew up in [[Liverpool]], and entered Trinity College, Cambridge in 1978, as one of the first women to enter the college.{{r|fountain}} She read mathematics there, entered graduate study at [[Louisiana State University]], returned to Cambridge for [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos]], and completed a Ph.D., on radio and molecular studies of the galactic centre, through Cambridge's [[Cavendish Laboratory]].{{r|engcam}}

Before taking her present position, she held a Junior Research Fellowship in [[Trinity Hall, Cambridge]] from 1987 until 1990, did a year of postdoctoral research at the [[Marconi Research Centre]], and held a Royal Society University Research Fellowship for research into Applications of Geometric Algebra in Engineering in [[Newnham College, Cambridge]], from 1994 until 2000.{{r|engcam}}

==Books==
Lasenby has edited two books on [[geometric algebra]]:
*''Applications of Geometric Algebra in Computer Science and Engineering'' (with Leo Dorst and Chris Doran, Springer, 2002)
*''Guide to Geometric Algebra in Practice'' (with Leo Dorst, Springer, 2011)
